cards.explanation: The answer is his brothers and all his sons. Jeremiah the prophet takes Jaazaniah, his brothers and all his sons, "…the entire house of the Rechabites…" (Jeremiah 35:3). The text says the ENTIRE house, friends, so nobody gets to sit this one out. That's a lot of folks to walk into one room.

The answer is that Jonadab told them never to drink it. The Rechabites say he commanded, "Neither you nor your descendants are ever to drink wine." (Jeremiah 35:6). Never means never, friends, and there's no loophole in that sentence. I've looked for loopholes in my own rules for years, and I respect this.

The answer is tents. Jonadab said, "…you must live in tents all your lives…" (Jeremiah 35:7). All their lives, friends, not just a camping weekend. I get nervous when my oven mitt goes missing, so I can't imagine a whole life with no walls.

The answer is so they could live a long time in the land. Jonadab says to live in tents "…so that you may live a long time in the land where you wander." (Jeremiah 35:7). That's the reason the text gives, so I'll stick to it. Sometimes a rule comes with its reason attached, friends, and that's a kindness.

The answer is True. The Rechabites say, "…we have not drunk wine all our lives…" (Jeremiah 35:8). They say that goes for their wives and their sons and daughters too. The whole household, friends, keeping one rule.

The answer is to escape the armies coming in. The Rechabites said, "Come, let us go into Jerusalem to escape the armies of the Chaldeans and the Arameans." (Jeremiah 35:11). So they went into Jerusalem to escape the armies, friends. That's the reason they gave.

The answer is that they have been carried out. God says, "The words of Jonadab son of Rechab have been carried out." (Jeremiah 35:14). He holds up the Rechabites as people who did what they were told. I think that's the kind of compliment you remember, friends.
The answer is False. God says, "…I have spoken to you again and again, and you have not obeyed Me!" (Jeremiah 35:14). So He spoke many times, friends, not once. The problem wasn't a lack of words.

The answer is to turn from their wicked ways. The prophets proclaimed, "Turn now, each of you, from your wicked ways, and correct your actions." (Jeremiah 35:15). God says He sent them again and again. And of the people He says, "…you have not inclined your ear or listened to Me."

The answer is gods, friends, GODS! The prophets said, "Do not go after other gods to serve them." (Jeremiah 35:15). Notice the two actions in that warning: going after them and serving them. It comes in the same message as turning from wicked ways.

The answer is disaster. God says, "…I will bring to Judah and to all the residents of Jerusalem all the disaster I have pronounced against them…" (Jeremiah 35:17). It's a heavy line, friends. He gives the reason too: "…I have spoken to them but they have not obeyed, and I have called to them but they have not answered."

The answer is a man to stand before God always. The LORD of Hosts says, "Jonadab son of Rechab will never fail to have a man to stand before Me." (Jeremiah 35:19). Because the Rechabites obeyed, that promise came to the family. I think that beats any trophy I could stamp, friends.
